$allowed_cells_comment: WHAT A CELL HAS TO BE FOR CHECK 1 TO ABSOLVE IT, AND WHY THESE COULD NOT BE.
A cell passes when it IS a declared string, when it is contained in one, or when it
tiles out of several. MIN_SLOT is 6, so a declared string shorter than that may not
stand in for a slot: a corpus hit on 'no' or '0' would be coincidence, and normalising
on it would erase the sentence rather than its values. Every sub-MIN_SLOT cell the
generator emits therefore has to be declared here by hand.
Three classes are declared below, and they are not equally strong:
1. LABELS — 'Located in', 'Origins', 'ADVANCEMENT CRITERIA', the BLN-CAP and BLN-VAL
row heads. Presentation text the engine authors, carrying no measurement. Declaring
them costs nothing this check defends.
2. SHORT TOKENS — '0', 'no', 'none', '—', '18', '44'. Counts and verdicts too short to
normalise. Declaring the digit is weaker than declaring a pattern and this mechanism
has no pattern form; a cell holding only a digit carries no normative text.
3. COMPOSED MEASUREMENTS — 'origins 1 · heads 1 · acyclic YES', '18/20', '0/44
artifacts record a predecessor', and the two cells naming the write set and the
protected set. These pin today's numbers, so the day a measurement moves this gate
fails until somebody reviews the new value. That is the intended cost: the
alternative is a generator composing sentences out of counts with nothing watching.
THE DURABLE REPAIR FOR CLASS 3 IS IN THE ENGINE, NOT HERE. A cell holding one value
traces to a record; a cell holding 'origins 1 · heads 1 · acyclic YES' is a sentence
the generator minted, which is the thing this framework exists to refuse. Splitting
those cells is a change to baseline_engine.py and to the shape of every table that
carries them, and it is recorded here rather than done silently.

required_projections.$why: a baseline that succeeds another must be named where succession and currency are recorded, or a superseded baseline keeps being cited as current
the dashboard is the aggregate view of what the baseline confers; a capability absent from it is a capability nothing reports as inherited
a validation absent from the report it is reported in is an unrun check that reads as passed

$required_projections_comment: TARGETED, NOT ALL_SURFACES, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE OBLIGATION. Every entry
below used to name ALL_SURFACES, which asserted that all 46 declared ids appear in all
seven surfaces. They do not and should not: these surfaces answer different questions,
so the obligation was unsatisfiable by construction and CHECK 3 stood permanently red
while protecting nothing. A check that cannot pass cannot fail informatively either.
The reference adopter shows the correct form. UCOS-UCTX-001 points at
`agent_surfaces[].surface` — a HOMOGENEOUS family whose members INV-CTX-13 measures
for divergence, so every member carrying every value is a true statement. ALL_SURFACES
is that same claim made against a heterogeneous set, where it is simply false.
Each collection is now bound to the surface that actually projects it, measured rather
than assumed: capabilities 20/20 in the dashboard, validations 26/26 in the validation
report, baselines 2/2 in the succession and currency registers. The obligation is now
both TRUE and LOAD-BEARING — dropping one capability from the dashboard fires CHECK 3,
which is exactly the producer-emits-less defect the check exists to catch.
The alternative was to write the missing ids into the six documents that do not carry
them. That would have been a generator minting normative text to satisfy its own
verifier, which is the first failure UFI's own header names.
